leonidas: Sparta, circa 480 BCE. Greek linen or bronze cuirass, bronze Corinthian helmet, round aspis, dory spear, red wool cloak. No Roman segmented armor, no fantasy leather harness. Portrait: mature bearded commander, helmet raised to reveal face.
hypatia: Alexandria, circa 400 CE, late Roman Egypt. Philosopher in modest linen tunic and himation, scrolls and geometric instruments, no telescope or modern equations. Portrait: mature Greek-speaking woman scholar, thoughtful face, simply pinned dark hair. The great Ptolemaic library is not shown as an intact institution in her lifetime.
imhotep: Egypt, Third Dynasty circa 2650 BCE. Old Kingdom linen kilts, copper tools, papyrus and stone architecture at Saqqara. No horses, war chariots, iron, New Kingdom battle dress or glass laboratory equipment. Portrait: non-royal Egyptian architect and official, close cap, linen, papyrus roll, no pharaonic crown. Later statues are iconographic references, not contemporary portraits.
dandolo: Venice and Constantinople, circa 1200 CE. Wool, silk, chain mail, medieval oared galleys. No tricorn, eighteenth-century carnival mask, or Renaissance flintlock. Portrait: elderly blind doge, subdued cloudy eyes, simple early ducal cap and red mantle, no eyepatch.
khan: Widukind, Saxony, eighth century CE. Saxon wool tunics, cloaks, seax knives, spears, round wood shields, mail for wealthy warriors. No horns, Mongol lamellar armor or Mongolian faces inferred from legacy ID. Portrait: mature Saxon noble, beard, wool cloak and mail, Weser beech woodland.
boudicca: Vercingetorix and Arverni, Gaul circa 52 BCE. Late La Tene mail, iron swords, long oval shields, simple helmets, torcs, wool tunics and trousers. No horned fantasy helmets or Scottish tartan. Portrait: adult Gallic man, moustache, torc, cloak, Alesia backdrop; not Boudicca.
nostradamus: Johann Friedrich Boettger, Dresden and Meissen circa 1708 CE. Baroque coats, linen cravats, natural or curled wigs, clay crucibles and early porcelain. No medieval wizard clothes or magic runes. Portrait: young male alchemist in early eighteenth-century dress holding a small plain white porcelain vessel; not Nostradamus.
jeanne: Hildegard of Bingen, Rupertsberg circa 1150 CE. Benedictine habits and veils, Romanesque architecture, wax tablets, parchment, medicinal garden. No fifteenth-century plate armor or Joan of Arc insignia. Portrait: mature abbess with white linen under-veil and dark outer veil, stylus and tablet.
ragnar: Wiprecht von Groitzsch and Mark Meissen circa 1100 CE. Mail hauberk, nasal helmet, kite shield, wool tunics, timber and Romanesque buildings. No Viking fantasy, no later plate armor. Portrait: mature Saxon count in mail and a plain wool mantle, land charter, no anachronistic late surcoat.
musashi: Ulrich von Liechtenstein and Styria, thirteenth century CE. Mail, great helms, surcoats, kite or early heater shields, tournament lances, no full fifteenth-century plate suit. No Japanese samurai. Portrait: knight and minnesinger, face visible, great helm with small Venus crest held at side. Codex Manesse is a later stylized source.
perikles: Athens circa 440 BCE. Classical Greek chiton and himation, bronze helmets, round aspis, early classical temples with restrained polychromy. Portrait: bearded Pericles with Corinthian helmet pushed up, based on established sculptural portrait type.
agrippa: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, Rome circa 30 BCE. Late Republican mail or bronze cuirass, Montefortino/Coolus-type helmets, oval scuta. No Imperial lorica segmentata, no medieval ships. Portrait: broad strong brow, short curly hair, clean shaven, restrained naval crown. Agrippa original Pantheon must not use Hadrian later dome.
amanirenas: Ahhotep I and Egypt circa 1550 BCE, late Second Intermediate Period/early Eighteenth Dynasty. Linen, gold and faience, wood hide shields, bows, bronze axes; chariots only where named. No Ptolemaic queen, Roman armor, or Nubian Amanirenas. Portrait: Egyptian queen with linen dress, restrained vulture headdress, gold fly pendants treated as traditional attribution; exact tomb ownership is debated.
anna: Anna Komnene, Constantinople circa 1120 CE. Byzantine silk, purple and gold textiles, codex manuscripts, mail/lamellar for soldiers, round shields, cross-domed churches. Hagia Sophia without Ottoman minarets. Portrait: mature Byzantine scholar princess, modest silk dress and veil, codex, no fantasy crown.
nezahualcoyotl: Texcoco and central Mexico, fifteenth century CE before conquest. Acolhua/Nahua cotton mantles, turquoise diadem, sandals, quilted cotton armor, chimalli shields, obsidian-edged macuahuitl. No steel, horses, European crowns, Maya architecture, or Plains feather warbonnets. Portrait: mature Nahua ruler with turquoise xiuhuitzolli diadem and fine cotton cloak, flower, Lake Texcoco.
masako: Theophanu, Ottonian Empire circa 980 CE. Byzantine-influenced silk and gold court dress, pearl diadem, Romanesque churches, parchment charters. No Japanese armor or late medieval Gothic forms. Portrait: young Byzantine-born empress in formal silk with pearl diadem, dignified, charter.
epaminondas: Thebes in Boeotia circa 371 BCE. Fourth-century Greek hoplite equipment, linen cuirass, round aspis, bronze pilos or Boeotian helmet. Portrait: adult bearded Theban commander with open Boeotian helmet and calm expression.
fabius: Quintus Fabius Maximus, Rome circa 217 BCE, middle Republic. Toga praetexta, oval shields, mail, Montefortino helmets, no Imperial segmented armor. Portrait: older Roman statesman, clean shaven, white toga with restrained purple border, rolling Italian hills.
mandukhai: Thusnelda and Cherusci, Germania circa 15 CE. Wool and linen, fibula brooches, round shields, spears, longhouses. No Mongol, Viking horned helmet, medieval castle or fantasy warrior corset. Portrait: adult Germanic noblewoman, pinned or braided hair, wool mantle with bronze brooch, forest.
baibars: Mamluk Egypt and Syria circa 1260 CE. Thirteenth-century mail, textile-covered lamellar where appropriate, conical helmets, lance, composite bow, patterned tunics. No sixteenth-century Ottoman armor or flintlocks. Portrait: mature Kipchak-origin sultan in cloth-wrapped conical helmet and mail, restrained turquoise accents, Cairo citadel.
zizka: Sebastien Le Prestre de Vauban, France circa 1695 CE. Late seventeenth-century long coats, breeches, periwigs, matchlock or flintlock muskets as appropriate, bastioned fortifications, gabions and cannon. No Hussite wagon fort or medieval knight. Portrait: mature engineer with long curled wig, cuirass and blue sash, fortress drawing, face inspired by period portrait tradition.
fuhao: Lady of Vix, Hallstatt Burgundy circa 500 BCE. Wool garments, bronze fibulae, gold torc around neck not on head, amber and lignite bracelets, bronze krater, wagon and Mont Lassois. No Chinese Shang imagery, no La Tene war fantasy. Portrait: mature woman with gold torc, patterned wool dress, amber ornaments. Name and exact face unknown; status as ruler is interpretive.
